what: TC Energy owns natural gas pipelines across North America, including the system that carries most of Canada's gas to markets, plus Mexican pipelines and power generation. It spun off its oil pipeline business as South Bow.
customers: Gas producers, utilities, power generators and industrial users in Canada, the United States and Mexico.
money: the NGTL system and Canadian Mainline
Columbia and ANR systems in the US Northeast and Midwest
long-haul pipelines serving Mexican power generation
moat: Pipeline corridors that would be impossible to build today, with capacity contracted on regulated or long-term terms.
risks: Debt of about $44 billion against under $1 billion of cash
The Coastal GasLink project ran far over budget
Large projects face long permitting and indigenous consultation processes
Rising rates raise the cost of refinancing
opportunities: Revenue grew about 16% last year with a 53% operating margin
Gas demand from power generation and liquefied natural gas exports is growing
A dividend yield near 4% backed by contracted cash flow
watch: Project costs against budget and the debt-to-EBITDA ratio.
